articles.title: From the Dealership to the Sportsbook: The Consumer Comes First
articles.deck: Josh King draws on his automotive background to explain how he wants to give consumers more leverage and a trusted advocate.
articles.author: Josh King
articles.label: By Josh King
articles.body:
Dear JKSportsBook fans,

This is your Executive Producer and founder reaching out.

If you've ever owned or driven a car, you know how expensive it can be. And let's be honest: dealerships take advantage of consumers every single day.

Have you ever noticed how friendly and attentive a salesperson is when you're buying a car, only for that same energy to disappear when you come back needing help? Suddenly, the calls aren't returned, the texts go unanswered, and you're no longer a priority.

I've seen it from the other side.

Throughout my media career, I worked with 15 different dealerships. They provided me with offices, vehicles, and cash to represent their brands. I eventually left the automotive industry after the pandemic, but I maintained close relationships with dealership owners, GMs, sales managers, and salespeople.

Here's what makes us different:

I'm not an independent agent working for the dealerships. I'm working for YOU.

I want to help you get the most money possible for your trade-in and secure the best deal on your next vehicle.

My compensation is simple: I ask each dealership to pay me a flat $500 referral fee. That's it. My fee doesn't increase based on how much you spend, what vehicle you buy, or how much profit the dealership makes. My incentive is to help YOU get the best possible deal.

The Eminem song Superman plays in my head as I walk you through the dealership. 😂

But here's what I know: dealerships come and go. Saturday through Sunday. Monday through Sunday. The car business never stops, and neither do we.

I'm preparing to partner with a major dealership, but until that happens, I'm continuing to help everyday people for 0% compensation from the consumer.

I have enough money. This isn't about squeezing another dollar out of you. It's about changing the way people buy cars and pushing back against dealerships and finance companies that take advantage of consumers.

When you or someone you know needs a car, reach out to JKSportsBook directly.

Q and I have made a decision: we're going to teach people how to fish instead of simply handing them a fish. We want to educate consumers, give them leverage, and show them how the car-buying process really works.

And we're not taking dealership blood money the way other sportsbooks do. F THAT.

Have a question about buying, selling, trading, or anything automotive-related? DM me on Instagram:

@joshking65

We're working around the clock.

It's time the consumer had somebody in their corner.

articles.title: The VIP Life Was Brutal. The Next Chapter Is Compliance.
articles.deck: Josh King reflects on life as a casino VIP, the cost of chasing an image, and the more transparent approach he plans to take in 2027.
articles.author: Josh King
articles.label: By Josh King
articles.body:
Dear JKSportsBook fans,

A lot of you ask me what it was really like living at MGM National Harbor.

Let me tell you... IT WAS BRUTAL. 😂

I couldn't stop eating Shake Shack and sushi every single day. It was freezing cold, and I was required to wager $1,000 per game, all while the casino was essentially hoping I'd lose.

I won the poker tournament, then proceeded to give most of those winnings back playing blackjack. When I finally walked out, I was up $7,000 but approximately 77 pounds heavier. (Okay, realistically, 40, but it FELT like 77.)

I ultimately decided to leave on my own.

Being a VIP sounds glamorous until you actually live it. The pressure, the expectations, the constant action... it can become exhausting.

I was also betting someone else's picks (Cooperinthe412), and I felt obligated to tip, pay out, and keep the whole thing moving. Looking back, it became a spiral of spending money for the sake of vanity and maintaining an image.

And that's something I want to be honest about.

I still believe in sports betting, but what I've always loved most is the media side of this business.

That's why I'm making a major change.

On January 1, 2027, I'm returning to gambling full-time, but this time with a different approach. I want to understand the tax code, learn the legitimate tax implications and potential benefits of gambling, and educate our audience along the way.

One word will define this next chapter:

COMPLIANCE.

I want everything we do to be aboveboard. That means understanding IRS requirements, keeping proper records, documenting everything, and making sure our other business endeavors are operating the right way, too.

I'm not interested in cutting corners. I'm interested in building something sustainable, transparent, and educational.

And trust me, the content is going to be AMAZING.

Between now and January 1, 2027, we'll be sharing some incredible behind-the-scenes media coverage from the past. You'll get to see a side of this industry that most people never experience.

Most importantly, I want to teach people how to fish for themselves.

If I've made mistakes along the way, I want you to learn from them. If I've experienced something firsthand, I want to share it. And if there's a better, smarter, and more responsible way to approach this business, we're going to explore it together.

This next chapter isn't just about gambling. It's about education, media, transparency, and building something bigger than ourselves.

Let's learn, grow, and fly together.

January 1, 2027. We're just getting started.
